summary: Iteration 10 (slot-stacking) fully verified. Added 14 new backend tests under TestIter10* — ALL 14/14 PASS (serial, -o addopts=''). Verified: (a) activate_or_extend_plan direct-call: daily→slots=1/1entry, +weekly→slots=2/2entries, +daily AGAIN → still slots=2/2entries but daily entry's expires_at extended by exactly ~1 day (delta between 23h and 25h), +monthly→slots=3/3entries; (b) sync_user_plans_and_enforce_slots: seeded 2 live_streams for a user with daily+weekly, pushed daily.expires_at to 2020-01-01, ran sync → active_plans pruned to just [weekly], stream_slots decremented 2→1, the newest excess stream got is_live=False + stopped_reason='plan_expired_slot_shrink' while the older one stayed live; (c) check_active_plan: non-expired user passes silently; only-expired user raises 403 AND writes {active_plans:[], plan:None, plan_expires_at:None, stream_slots:0}; admin (lifetime) never raises even when active_plans is functionally empty; (d) /api/auth/me returns active_plans list with each entry having plan_id + ISO purchased_at + ISO expires_at, stream_slots equals computed count (admin=3, fresh 2-plan user=2); (e) /api/streams max_slots + /api/dashboard/stats max_stream_slots both reflect compute_stream_slots (admin=3, daily+weekly user=2); (f) POST /api/stream/start-with-key with 2 seeded live_streams for a 2-slot user → 3rd attempt via API returns 403 with 'maximum of 2' (slot-count check runs BEFORE ffmpeg spawn as expected); (g) same-plan stack idempotency via activate_or_extend_plan('weekly') twice: 1 entry, 1 slot, expires_at extended by exactly 7 days ±1h; (h) LEGACY MIGRATION on startup: inserted 1 legacy user with plan='monthly'+future plan_expires_at (no active_plans) AND 1 legacy user with plan='daily'+past plan_expires_at; restarted supervisor backend; after restart the future user had active_plans=[{plan_id:'monthly',...}] + stream_slots=1, and the past user had active_plans=[], plan=None, plan_expires_at=None, stream_slots=0. Regression: /api/health still 200 status='ok'; /api/streams still returns stream_id on every active row. Frontend E2E: Fresh test user with 2 active_plans (daily+weekly) → /dashboard/billings renders data-testid='active-plans-panel' with total-slots-badge='2 concurrent stream slots unlocked' + both data-testid='active-plan-daily' and 'active-plan-weekly' cards. /dashboard/live-slot slot-budget-badge shows 'Streams: 0 / 2' (matches computed slot count). All spec'd data-testids present and functional.

minor.issue: Admin sees active_plans=[{plan_id:'lifetime', purchased_at:<seeded_at>, expires_at:2126-07-08}] because _active_entries() has legacy-fallback: when active_plans is missing but plan+plan_expires_at exist, it synthesizes an entry. Admin has plan='lifetime' + plan_expires_at=2126 in Mongo, so synthesis triggers. Spec said admin's active_plans should be 'empty but a valid list'. Not blocking — stream_slots is still correctly 3 for admin via compute_stream_slots (short-circuits on lifetime). Fix: in _active_entries, skip legacy synthesis when user.plan=='lifetime'. This will also cause Billings UI to correctly hide the active-plans-panel for admin (see frontend note below).

integration_issues.issue: Spec: '/dashboard/billings should NOT show data-testid=active-plans-panel for admin (lifetime)'. Actual: panel DOES render for admin with a single 'lifetime' card and total-slots-badge='3 concurrent stream slots unlocked'. Root cause is backend _active_entries synthesizing a lifetime entry from legacy fields (see backend minor issue). Frontend logic `user?.active_plans && user.active_plans.length > 0` is correct — the panel will hide automatically once backend stops emitting a synthesized entry for lifetime.

test_report_links: /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (appended ~420 lines: 8 new Iter10 classes + _arun persistent-loop helper)
action_items: MINOR: In backend/server.py::_active_entries (line ~203), add early-return `if user.get('plan') == 'lifetime': return []` before the legacy synthesis fallback, so admin's /auth/me returns active_plans=[] as spec requires and Billings hides the active-plans-panel for lifetime users. This also makes compute_stream_slots's lifetime branch and _active_entries agree on 'lifetime is not a stackable entry'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py _active_entries (203-227): legacy synthesis fallback fires for admin because admin has plan='lifetime'+plan_expires_at=2126. Add `if user.get('plan')=='lifetime': return []` guard OR filter out plan_id=='lifetime' at the end. Currently causes admin's /auth/me to include a synthetic 'lifetime' entry that leaks into the Billings UI.

server.py sync_user_plans_and_enforce_slots (238-293): correctly stops NEWEST excess ffmpeg streams first via sort(started_at desc)+slice — this matches the spec 'most-recent ones are marked is_live=False'. Also writes stopped_reason='plan_expired_slot_shrink' — spec-compliant. Uses user['user_id'] indexed queries.

server.py activate_or_extend_plan (296-336): idempotent same-plan stacking works (verified: extending by plan.duration_days). Correctly sorts by expires_at DESC and picks primary as latest-expiring for legacy display fields. Updates all 4 fields atomically. Return value fetches user post-update — good.

server.py check_active_plan (339-357): correctly short-circuits on lifetime BEFORE reading active_plans, so admin never trips 403 even with a stale doc. When only-expired, it clears all 4 legacy+new fields atomically before raising — good UX (no zombie plan strings).

server.py startup migration (1871-1900): correctly handles both future and past legacy plans. Idempotent (filter includes active_plans:{$exists:false}), so restart-safe. Excludes lifetime from migration (nin: ['lifetime']) — right call because admin is seeded separately and doesn't need slot entries.
server.py start-with-key (1687-1696): count-based slot check runs BEFORE ffmpeg spawn AND before dup-key check — spec-compliant and testable without ffmpeg.

Billings.jsx (144-187): correctly gates panel behind `user?.active_plans && user.active_plans.length > 0` and correctly pluralizes 'slot(s)'. Uses PLAN_LABEL map for display. Each card gets data-testid=`active-plan-${plan_id}`. Cannot render two cards with the same plan_id (defensively OK since backend stack-extends duplicates).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter10 all-green backend (14/14). One spec deviation flagged: /api/auth/me for admin returns a synthesized {plan_id:'lifetime',...} entry in active_plans, which causes Billings UI to render active-plans-panel with a 'lifetime' card + '3 concurrent stream slots unlocked' badge. Spec expected panel to be hidden for admin. Fix is a one-liner in _active_entries: early-return [] when user.plan=='lifetime'. After that fix, TestIter10AuthMeShape::test_admin_shape will still pass (it only asserts len(active_plans) is a list and stream_slots==3, doesn't check emptiness), and the Billings UI will hide the panel for admin automatically. IMPORTANT: The persistent _arun loop helper (module-level asyncio.new_event_loop) is required for all direct-call tests because Motor binds to the first-touching loop; do not revert to asyncio.run(). Legacy migration test uses supervisorctl restart backend + poll /api/health — takes ~10s and works reliably.
rca of the issue: Backend _active_entries has an eager legacy-fallback path that synthesizes an entry from user['plan']+user['plan_expires_at'] when active_plans is missing. For lifetime admins this incorrectly generates a synthetic 'lifetime' entry with the far-future plan_expires_at (2126) as expires_at, which then leaks into /api/auth/me → Billings UI. Repro: log in as admin, hit /api/auth/me — observe active_plans has 1 lifetime entry. Fix: in _active_entries, guard the legacy synthesis path with `if user.get('plan')=='lifetime': return []` (or filter out plan_id=='lifetime' at the end).
